A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Direct Coverage Optimization work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including content relocated in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original mathematical-answering and theorem-proving experiments, including confidence analyses, larger-model results, AIME24 evaluation, and expert iteration.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds GRPO results and confidence analyses on MATH.

M1.justification: The DCO loss and confidence factor, step-wise DCO, Monte Carlo approximation DCOa, and example-replacement procedure are retained. GRPO is an added comparator, not a new proposed component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MATH direct answers and chain-of-thought reasoning, AIME24 evaluation, and Mathlib/LeanDojo and MiniF2F theorem proving. The GRPO experiment uses the existing MATH reasoning task.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GRPO alongside CE as a comparator for DCOa. Appendix B specifies Dr. GRPO modifications to its implementation. Comparator membership in the other experiments is retained.

E3.justification: The added GRPO experiment introduces eight rollouts per problem, batch size 128, five epochs, a 1e-6 learning rate, batch balancing, and an R1 prompt with strict formatting requirements. Previously reported DCO and theorem-proving settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3(c,d) adds analyses of GRPO confidence over training and the correctness of highly confident answers. The easy-data analysis moves from Section 4.4 to Appendix C.1; existing robustness, calibration, and expert-iteration analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 continues reporting standard errors of the mean, and the new GRPO entries use that existing convention. No new independent-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds nine GRPO entries in Table 3 and associated confidence findings. For example, epoch-five GRPO scores are 14.6±0.1 at pass@1 and 35.4±0.3 at pass@64. Existing CE/DCOa entries and Tables 1, 2, and 4–6 retain their values.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly defines the modified GRPO surrogate objective and centered-reward advantages. This is a limited mathematical addition for the comparator; the DCO derivation, confidence lemmas, and Appendix A proofs retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the claims about CE/pass@N misalignment, overconfidence, DCO, and its theorem-proving and reasoning extensions. The central conclusion about aligning training with test-time strategies is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 extends the overconfidence interpretation to the tested GRPO implementation. Section 6 replaces the earlier future-work outlook with explicit limitations concerning verifier availability, mathematical-domain coverage, and the limited investigation of RL methods.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds GRPO implementation details, its prompt and reward specification, dataset licenses, and per-run GPU-hour estimates for DCO variants. Existing hardware information and the promised code location are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning around GRPO and recent RL reasoning studies, citing Yue et al. (2025), Liu et al. (2025), and Zeng et al. (2025). The Zhang et al. (2024) speciality-versatility reference is removed; the principal positioning against earlier work remains.

P1.justification: Related-work and several method/results paragraphs are condensed, Section 4.4 moves to Appendix C.1, and the closing outlook is rewritten. The title, central narrative, and main six-section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 Figures 4, 3, and 5 are consolidated into v3 Figure 2; the CoT figure gains GRPO panels, Tables 2 and 3 are reorganized, and the easy-data figure moves into the appendix. This substantially restructures the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the existing study with a documented RL comparator, confidence diagnostics, explicit applicability limits, and concrete computational costs. These improve evidential breadth and transparency while preserving the original results. The gain remains limited because the added empirical comparison concerns one GRPO configuration on the existing MATH task.
